publisher: Frontex (European Border and Coast Guard Agency)
title: Irregular border crossings down 40% in Q1 2026
key_claim: Irregular border crossings into EU fell 39-40% YoY in Q1 2026, ~21,400 detections. Western African route down 83%; Eastern Mediterranean down 34% (~6,500 detections); Central Mediterranean down 33% (~6,200); Western Mediterranean only major route to increase (+66%, ~4,400).
notes: Primary EU regulator data — quantification anchor for the European side of the inflow collapse.

title: Macroeconomic implications of immigration flows in 2025 and 2026: January 2026 update
key_claim: US net migration estimated at -295,000 to -10,000 for 2025 — the first negative net migration in at least half a century. 2026 projected range -925,000 to +185,000. Sustainable monthly job growth 20,000-50,000 in late 2025, could go negative in 2026. Consumer spending reduction $60-110B combined 2025-2026. CBO comparison estimates +400,000 for 2025; CPS-based Pew / Center for Immigration Studies estimates suggest larger -1.5M to -2M drop in foreign-born population.
notes: Tier 2 anchor for the US side of the inflow collapse. Authors Edelberg, Veuger, Watson — top institutional credibility.

title: The global race for talent: Other nations are outpacing the U.S. on high-skill immigration
key_claim: Trump administration imposing $100,000 H-1B fee from September 2025 (previously $2,000-$5,000); 2004 H-1B cap cut from 195,000 to 65,000 increased multinational employment to overseas locations (Canada, China, India); Berenberg lowered US growth estimate from 2% to 1.5% after H-1B fee. US first-time international student enrollment fell 17% in Fall 2025. Canada, Australia, UK, Singapore expanding high-skill visa regimes; UK Graduate Visa, Australia's Temporary Graduate Visa, Canada's Post-Graduate Work Permit; Singapore COMPASS framework.
notes: STRUCTURAL ANCHOR — canonical framing of the H-1B fee shock and peer-economy responses. At 6 months exactly, within window.

publisher: ICEF Monitor (NAFSA, Oxford Test of English, Studyportals Global Enrolment Benchmark Survey)
title: Universities urged to focus on 'factors they can control' as policy settings depress international student enrolments in the Big Four
key_claim: Q1 2026 Global Enrolment Benchmark Survey: 69% of Canadian universities reported fewer new undergraduates (after 82% in Q1 2025 — two years severe contraction). 62% of US universities welcomed fewer new undergraduates (up from 48% in Q1 2025). 44% of Australian institutions reported declines; UK 42%. In contrast, 82% of Asian institutions saw MORE new undergraduates in Q1 2026, 47% of European universities reported increases. 80% of Canadian postgraduate programmes reported declines; 55% of Asian universities reported postgraduate gains. Restrictive policy cited as top barrier by 100% of Australian, 84% of US/Canadian, 71% of UK responding institutions.
notes: The canonical recent evidence base for the Big Four enrolment reversal and Asia-Europe pickup. Quality industry-data trade press.

title: U.S. Sees 20% Drop in New International Students
key_claim: F-1 student visas issued May-August 2025 fell 36% vs same period 2024. New US international student enrollment fell 20% in 2025. Trump administration imposed travel bans for 12+ countries; new student visa restrictions and vetting rules; H-1B applications more onerous and expensive.
notes: Quality journalism — anchor for the Anglo policy shock on student inflows.

title: India looks to reverse brain drain amid US uncertainty
key_claim: 30% rise in Ivy League Indian graduates seeking positions in India following US visa uncertainty. India hosts 1,600+ Global Capability Centres employing 1.66 million people. VAJRA (Visiting Advanced Joint Research) and GATI schemes target diaspora scientific talent. Immigration restriction anxieties plus reduced US federal grants persuading early-career Indian scientists and engineers to rethink US careers.
notes: Quality regional analysis on the reverse-brain-drain corridor. Treat directionally — opinion piece quoting agreed numbers.

title: IOM Report: Migration Drives Economies and Development, but Gains Are at Risk (World Migration Report 2026)
key_claim: World Migration Report 2026: international migrants reached 304 million in 2024, 3.7% of global population; remittances $905B in 2024; South-Asia-to-Middle-East now world's largest South-South corridor (21.5M migrants); China population decline starts in 2026; migration shifting toward South-South corridors as Anglosphere closes.
notes: International authoritative source on world migration trends; counter-anchor for the structural framing.
